seo_title: Cost of Living in Malaga 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Malaga per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of the Costa del Sol: around 300 sunny days, mild winters and a reputation as one of Spain's most comfortable cities for families. You relocate via a digital nomad visa or a residence permit, and a stable income is required.
pros: Around 300 sunny days and a mild winter on the Mediterranean
One of the most comfortable and safest cities in Spain for families
Widespread English, an airport hub and the high-speed AVE train
A digital nomad visa with a 24% tax rate (the Beckham regime)
Beaches, mountains and all of Andalusia close by
cons: A Schengen visa and income from about €2,850 a month for the nomad visa
NIE and empadronamiento bureaucracy and queues for cita previa
Rent is expensive and rising fast due to tourism and expats
Spanish is needed for paperwork and outside the tourist areas
Very hot and crowded on the coast in summer

best_places.name: Old Town (Centro Histórico)
best_places.description: A pedestrian centre with the cathedral, the Picasso Museum and cafés on every corner.

best_places.name: La Malagueta
best_places.description: The city beach and promenade a step from the centre — popular with newcomers.

best_places.name: Pedregalejo and El Palo
best_places.description: Former fishing quarters by the sea, with chiringuitos and a relaxed atmosphere.

best_places.name: Teatinos
best_places.description: A modern district by the university — new builds, cheaper than the centre, handy with kids.

visa_steps.title: Digital nomad visa or residence permit
visa_steps.description: A Digital Nomad Visa for remote workers (income from about €2,850/month) or a non-lucrative visa for the financially independent.

visa_steps.title: NIE
visa_steps.description: A foreigner's identification number — needed for everything: the bank, renting, contracts.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: BBVA, Santander, CaixaBank or Sabadell open accounts with a passport and a NIE.

visa_steps.title: Rental and empadronamiento
visa_steps.description: A lease and registration at the town hall (padrón) — needed for the residence permit and access to healthcare.

visa_steps.title: Residence card (TIE)
visa_steps.description: After arrival — biometrics and the TIE card; the first term is usually 1–3 years, renewable.

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Malaga?
faq.answer: Yes, Spain is in Schengen. To live there you obtain a digital nomad visa or a non-lucrative (financially independent) visa.

faq.question: How much money do you need to move to Malaga?
faq.answer: For the nomad visa — a stable income from about €2,850 a month for one person; for the non-lucrative — savings and passive income.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Malaga?
faq.answer: Mediterranean and very mild: around 300 sunny days, a warm winter and a hot summer.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Malaga?
faq.answer: No, cards from Russia don't work. You need an account and card from a Spanish bank, which require a NIE.

faq.question: Is Malaga good with children?
faq.answer: Yes, the city is safe, with the sea, parks and international schools — one of families' favourite destinations.

faq.question: What about work in Malaga?
faq.answer: The local market requires Spanish; relocators on a nomad visa work remotely. The IT cluster at Málaga TechPark is growing.

reviews.text: We got the nomad visa, with a 24% tax under the Beckham regime — nice. Malaga is sunny and convenient, but finding a rental took a while and wasn't cheap.
We moved with our child: the sea, safety, an international school. The downside — Spanish bureaucracy and the queues for cita previa.
